To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the speed of sound for both axial and bending waves in elastic rods and beams is higher when finite strain is incorporated than when infinitesimal strain is assumed and (2) for bending waves in beams, the speed of sound is significantly higher for inextensional planer motion than it is for conventional transverse motion.

the effect of finite deformation in the dispersion of elastic waves in rods and beams, and the implications for wave motion in nonlinearly deforming media.

The main takeaway from our work is that

finite deformation must be taken into account in order to obtain accurate results for the dispersion relation, especially when large amplitude motion is involved, as it may lead to significant errors in the prediction of the phase and group velocity of elastic waves.
